findings.reason: the plan must either route the converted description through the existing publish/resolve owner (with a JT-60SA pin) or state in §4 why the per-phase netCDF is a distinct artifact class that owner cannot hold, because a forked description store silently splits the spine's machine-provenance into two mechanisms.
findings.text: §4 persists the converted JT-60SA description as per-phase IDS netCDF under `JT60SA_ROOT/machine_description/` carrying a "deck hash receipt", but the content-addressed machine-description artifact store — `publish_object`, `resolve_machine_description`, pinned physical/registry/semantic digests, `CACHE_ENV`/`DIGEST_ENV` — already exists in `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py` and is consumed by the spine through `imas_ambix/gs/machine_selection.py:192 select_machine`; the plan never names that owner, so the spine would receive JT-60SA geometry through a second provenance/receipt path beside the one the spine's other machines use

findings.reason: naming the owner turns §4's done-when into a reuse of existing assertions (extend them for the JT-60SA phases) instead of an invitation to rebuild determinism and boundary-change checks already proven for MAST's two geometry transitions.
findings.text: §4's done-when requires "the three identity assertions (determinism, partition consistency, visible change at the OP1/OP2 boundary)" but does not cite the module that already implements them (`machine_description_bytes`, `geometry_description_for_transition`, `description_field_changes`), so the node reads as re-deriving checks ambix already owns

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each new surface (§2 exporter, §3 extractor, §7 EQDB reader) hides substantial behaviour (ssh transport, unit/sign/COCOS collapse, EQDB record parsing) behind one function or one fetch entry, and §7 shares the §3 transport rather than adding a parallel path.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 lands a second machine-description store with its own "deck hash receipt" while `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py` already owns the content-addressed, pinned, receipted machine-description artifact store.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 ("retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"), §3 ("retires nothing, because ambix has no remote reader today"; "adds no ambix data command") and §7 ("retires nothing, because no equilibrium-database reader exists in ambix") each account for their surface in-text, and §5 adds data rather than a definition family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searches and cites the machine-map, transform-engine, view, signal-map and spine machinery it extends, but not `imas_ambix/data/description_identity.py`, which already owns the boundary/identity assertions §4 lists as a done-when.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two wrappers over existing/external machinery carry the required justification: §3 states importing imas-codex's remote layer would make its graph/LLM/tool-install dependencies a dependency of every ambix read, §4 extends NetCDFTransformEngine rather than adding an engine because a static description has no per-shot cost to amortise.
